text:
anya: heads-up — we finished the hot-cache pruning experiment on the helix fleet this morning. short summary below, will expand if folks want details. :tada:

ops-bot: deploy: rollout hot-cache-prune v2 -> helix-canary (10 hosts) at 2026-03-21T09:12:03Z

drew: quick numbers from the canary vs baseline (same traffic slice, 6hr run):
- p50: 48ms -> 46ms (≈4% better)
- p95: 210ms -> 150ms (≈29% better)
- p99: 430ms -> 320ms (≈26% better)
- token-cost per 1M tokens: $12.8 -> $11.9 (≈7% improvement)

chris: nice. did you see any regressed slices? cold starts or long-context traces?

anya: yes — small regressions for very sparse KV-hit scenarios (avg increase on cold p5 about +40ms) where evict happened between warmup and first long-request. overall user-facing tails improved though.

sam: can you paste the pruning config you used? curious about thresholds.

anya: sure — copied from the canary config:

```
configs.hot_cache_prune:
  enabled: true
  target_utilization: 0.72
  evict_interval_ms: 3000
  min_hold_ms: 15000
  max_evict_batch: 128
  prefer_prefix_stable: true
```

drew: implementation notes: the pruning algorithm prefers evicting low-reuse prefix entries first and keeps a tiny warmset for recent large KV entries. this reduced write-amplification and improved kernel scheduling under high concurrency.

sre_lead: any anomalies in error rates? I checked SLOs during canary window — 5xx flat, RT overall improved. but saw 1.2% increase in circuit-breaker hits for one customer shard. we rolled that shard back from v2.

anya: yeah that shard had unusually bursty long-context batches that triggered aggressive eviction. fix is to add a per-shard min_hold override. action item: add shard-level override and run an extended canary.

chris: what about the fallback plan? if we flip globally and see regressions.

drew: fallback is simple — toggle configs.hot_cache_prune.enabled=false, servers will stop background evictions and revert to previous passive decay. rollout-controlled via feature flags (one API call).

anya: next steps proposal:
1) add per-shard min_hold_ms override (PR queued)
2) extended canary on additional 50 hosts for 24h with traffic mix including long-context traces
3) update rollout playbook with rollback steps and customer-shard pinning command
4) monitor p99, cold p5, and circuit-breaker hits during canary and first 48h of roll

ops-bot: ticket created: RT-4521 — hot-cache pruning shard overrides + canary (assignee: anya)

sam: thanks — big win on tails and unit cost. please tag me in the PR for the override so I can sanity-check the defaults. :+1:

anya: will do. publishing a short note in #eng-runtime summary channel after extended canary completes unless anyone objects.

chris: no objections. also suggest a short bench doc for on-call — how to repro local regressed case (bench-run args, logs to collect).

anya: adding that to the ticket now. sample bench cmd we used:
```
bench-run --model redwood-13b --warmup 250 --samples 2000 --mix long_context:0.15 --kv-hit-prob 0.07
```

drew: tl;dr: strong p95/p99 tail reduction, modest cost savings, small cold-case regressions we can mitigate with per-shard overrides. ready for extended canary when infra approves.

sre_lead: approved for extended canary. please keep me looped and add dashboard links in the ticket.

anya: thx all — will follow up with canary results later today. :rocket:
